job.title: Care Home Manager
job.description:
Care Home Manager
Location: Māori Hill, Dunedin
Salary: $110,000–$125,000 + 10% Short-Term Incentive
Hours: Monday to Friday, 9 am–5 pm

We are seeking an experienced Care Home Manager to lead a well-established 50-bed aged care facility in Māori Hill, Dunedin, providing both rest home and hospital-level care. This is an exciting opportunity to take ownership of a service with a strong foundation, an established team and a collaborative working environment.

About the Role
As Care Home Manager, you will oversee clinical and operational performance, financial management, regulatory compliance and team leadership. You will play a key role in fostering a positive team culture, building strong relationships with residents and whānau, and ensuring the facility continues to thrive as a home our residents are proud to live in. Working alongside an established Clinical Manager and supportive leadership team, you will lead a multidisciplinary team of approximately 60 staff across nursing, caregiving, administration, kitchen, housekeeping, activities and maintenance.
Your responsibilities will include:

  • Providing strong, visible leadership across the facility.
  • Supporting and developing a collaborative, engaged workforce.
  • Ensuring high standards of resident care, safety and service delivery.
  • Maintaining operational oversight and ensuring the smooth running of a 24-hour care environment.
  • Building positive relationships with residents, whānau, families and staff.
  • Supporting continuous improvement and maintaining quality and compliance standards.
  • Managing financial performance and operational resources.
  • Empowering your team and fostering a positive, people-first culture.

About You
We are looking for someone who is genuinely passionate about people and understands that great care starts with great leadership.
You will ideally bring:

  • Experience in aged residential care, healthcare or a related sector.
  • Proven leadership and people management experience.
  • Strong financial and commercial acumen.
  • The ability to manage competing priorities in a complex environment.
  • A proven ability to build and maintain positive relationships with residents, whānau, families, staff and external stakeholders.
  • Excellent communication, interpersonal and problem-solving skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead change, motivate teams and drive continuous improvement.
  • A genuine passion for delivering exceptional care and service.

Why Consider This Opportunity?
This is an opportunity to join a facility with a strong and established team, where collaboration and empowerment are genuinely valued.
You'll enjoy:

  • A competitive salary open to negotiation depending on experience
  • An additional 10% short-term incentive.
  • Consistent Monday–Friday working hours, 9 am–5 pm.
  • An established Clinical Manager and experienced team around you.
  • A robust on-call structure, with after-hours involvement generally limited to emergencies.
  • The opportunity to make a meaningful impact on residents, staff and the wider service.

Interested? If you're a people-focused aged care leader ready for your next opportunity, we'd love to hear from you.

Know someone suitable? We offer a $500 referral bonus for successful referrals.

job.title: Facility Manager
job.description:
Residential Aged Care

About the role
If you enjoy running a service well and getting to know the people who make it work, this is an opportunity to do both. As Facility Manager, you’ll lead the day-to-day operations of a residential aged care facility in Whangārei that provides hospital-level and rest home care.

You’ll work closely with the Clinical Nurse Manager, who leads the clinical team. Together, you’ll provide clear, consistent leadership across the facility, making sure staffing and resources support residents’ needs and the team has what it needs to do its best work.
What you’ll be doing

  • Manage the facility’s day-to-day financial performance, including budgets, labour costs and expenditure.
  • Oversee staffing, rostering and payroll, and support recruitment and onboarding.
  • Lead enquiries, tours, admissions and sales to maintain strong occupancy and the right balance of hospital-level and rest home admissions.
  • Build relationships with residents, whānau and referral partners, and help prospective residents and their families make informed decisions about care.
  • Partner with the Clinical Nurse Manager on service quality, audit readiness, health and safety, and improvements across the facility.
  • Participate in a rotating on-call roster.

What you’ll bring

  • Proven experience managing a residential aged care facility or a comparable care service.
  • Confidence managing budgets, staffing costs, rosters and day-to-day operations.
  • An understanding of how occupancy, resident care needs and staffing affect facility performance.
  • A practical, approachable leadership style and the ability to build a strong working partnership with clinical leaders.
  • A current driver licence.

Apply in confidence If you’re ready to take ownership of a facility and build a service that residents, whānau and staff feel good about, we’d love to hear from you.

job.title: General Practitioner - GPEP 1 & 2 or Fellow considered
job.description:
About the organisation

Our client is an established New Zealand owned primary healthcare provider with practices across the country. It holds Trust status so profits go back into its clinics, people and services, rather than a return to shareholders. Local leaders have the flexibility to respond to their communities.

These two Wellington region practices combine the support of a national organisation with the relationships and familiarity of a local team. Experienced clinical, nursing and administration leaders work together to support patient care and the day-to-day running of each practice.

About the job and you

Join a permanent general practice role in Wellington CBD or Lower Hutt, with the option to work across both locations.

The Wellington CBD practice has approximately 3,000 enrolled patients and a generally well population. The Lower Hutt practice supports approximately 7,000-7,500 patients, including a significant high-needs population, offering varied clinical work and meaningful continuity of care.

You will provide broad general practice care, build relationships with patients and contribute to a collaborative clinical team. Sessions allow approximately three hours of patient-facing appointments and one hour of administration, with flexibility around appointment structure.

We are interested in GPs who bring:

  • Broad general practice experience and a patient-centred approach.
  • Confidence managing varied presentations across the lifespan.
  • A collaborative style and willingness to contribute to the wider team.
  • An interest in building long-term relationships within the community.

Fellowship is welcomed, although GPs who require supervision are also encouraged to enquire. An experienced Fellow and Clinical Lead provides mentoring and support across both practices.

Benefits of working here

  • Rates from $125 per hour.
  • Part-time opportunities of approximately 0.6-0.8 FTE.
  • Choice of Wellington CBD, Lower Hutt or work across both practices.
  • Protected administration time within clinical sessions.
  • Accessible clinical leadership and an established operational support team.
  • A car park provided at the Lower Hutt practice.
  • Enjoy Wellington's cafés, coastline, walking tracks and cycling, with time to make the most of them.

To find out more, contact Jeanette Rendle at RWR Health ph 027 705 7079 for a confidential conversation, or apply with your CV.

job.title: Clinical Director Napier (GP Fellow)
job.description:
About the opportunity

Are you an experienced GP ready to take the next step into clinical leadership, or an established GP leader looking for a new opportunity in beautiful Hawke’s Bay?

We are partnering with The Doctors Napier Group to appoint a Clinical Director to provide clinical leadership across three well-established practices in Napier, Greenmeadows and Ahuriri.

With approximately 23,800 enrolled patients, a stable team of experienced GPs and strong operational support, this is an opportunity to join a successful group of practices with excellent foundations already in place.

You don't necessarily need to have held a Clinical Director title before. What matters is your ability to bring people together, support your colleagues and champion high-quality patient care.

About the role

Working across the three practices, you'll play a key role in shaping clinical standards, supporting your fellow GPs and contributing to the ongoing success of the group.

This is a hands-on clinical leadership position where you'll continue seeing patients while having dedicated time to focus on leadership, mentoring and quality improvement.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Providing approachable, supportive clinical leadership across all three practices.
  • Championing clinical excellence, health equity and continuous quality improvement.
  • Mentoring and supporting GPs, including those earlier in their careers and internationally trained doctors.
  • Navigating clinical challenges, providing constructive feedback and supporting colleagues to deliver their best.
  • Working alongside experienced GP owners, practice managers and the wider clinical team to identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Contributing to clinical strategy and helping shape efficient, effective ways of delivering primary care.

There is also the opportunity to be involved in GP teaching and supervision, depending on your interests and experience.

About you

We're looking for a capable, approachable GP who enjoys working with people and has the confidence to lead by example. You'll bring sound clinical judgement, excellent communication skills and the ability to build trust and credibility with experienced colleagues. You'll be comfortable having challenging conversations when needed, while maintaining a collaborative and supportive approach.

Ideally, you'll offer:

  • FRNZCGP and vocational registration with the Medical Council of New Zealand, or recognised equivalent specialist GP fellowship.
  • Strong clinical experience in New Zealand general practice or a comparable setting.
  • An interest in clinical leadership, mentoring and developing others.
  • Experience or enthusiasm for clinical governance, quality improvement and teaching.
  • The ability to engage and influence colleagues across multiple practice locations.
  • Legal eligibility to work in New Zealand.

Previous formal leadership experience would be advantageous, but we're equally interested in hearing from experienced GP Fellows who are ready to take that next step.

What's on offer?

  • Attractive remuneration - happy to discuss with you
  • 8–10 sessions per week, with flexibility around your working arrangements.
  • Dedicated clinical leadership time alongside your patient consultations.
  • Three established, well-performing practices with strong patient enrolments.
  • Experienced GP colleagues, including teaching GPs and practice owners.
  • Excellent nursing, administration and operational support.
  • Professional development, career progression and the benefits of being part of a wider healthcare network.

The Doctors Napier Group is now part of the growing Tend network, bringing together established primary care expertise with innovative technology and new approaches to healthcare delivery.

Why Hawke's Bay?

Enjoy the lifestyle that comes with living in one of New Zealand's most desirable regions. Hawke's Bay offers beautiful beaches, award-winning wineries, excellent schools, a thriving food and arts scene, and an enviable climate. Whether you're relocating or already call the region home, it's a fantastic place to build your career and enjoy life outside work.

Interested? If you're an experienced GP who enjoys supporting others and would welcome the opportunity to influence clinical care across a successful group of practices, we'd love to hear from you.

For a confidential conversation, contact Jeanette Rendle at RWR Health Ph 027 705 7079, or apply online.

job.title: Pharmacist
job.description:
Pharmacist - Independent Community Pharmacy
Ashburton, Canterbury | $55-$65 per hour | Full-time
An exciting opportunity has become available for a Pharmacist to join a well-established, independently owned community pharmacy in Ashburton.
This is a great opportunity for a Pharmacist looking to join a friendly, supportive team, enjoy a good level of autonomy and potentially progress into a senior leadership or management position.

The owner is open to considering Pharmacists with 2+ years' experience, and the role can be tailored to suit the successful candidate's experience, strengths and career aspirations.

The Opportunity

  • Full-time position, 40 hours per week.
  • Salary ranging from $55-$65 per hour, depending on experience and level of responsibility.
  • Opportunity to step into a Dispensary Manager or Pharmacy Manager position.
  • Scope to take on wider management responsibilities, including staff rostering, administration and general pharmacy operations.
  • Potential for future ownership or a buy-in opportunity for someone interested in becoming more involved in the business long term.
  • Opportunity to introduce new services and help grow the pharmacy's presence within the local community.
  • Relocation assistance available for candidates moving to the area.

About the Pharmacy
This is a busy, largely dispensary-based independent pharmacy, dispensing approximately 8,500-9,000 prescriptions per month.
The pharmacy operates with:

  • 2 Pharmacist FTE.
  • Approximately 3 full-time equivalent Pharmacy Technicians.
  • A well-established and friendly team.
  • Vaccination services and additional community pharmacy offerings.

The pharmacy has a strong existing customer base and a supportive owner who values open communication, staff development and new ideas.
Unlike a corporate environment, you'll have the opportunity to influence how the pharmacy operates, develop new services and make a genuine contribution to its future direction.

Hours & Roster

  • 40 hours per week.
  • Opening hours: Monday-Friday, 8:30am-6:00pm.
  • Saturday morning opening.
  • Saturday mornings are preferred, but not compulsory. There is flexibility around the roster, with time off during the week to compensate where applicable.
  • Potential to work 9:00am-6:00pm with a one-hour lunch break.

Salary & Benefits

  • $55-$65 per hour, depending on experience and responsibilities.
  • Professional registration fees and educational fees paid.
  • Additional training and professional development supported and funded.
  • Annual bonus, typically paid around Christmas.
  • Annual performance and salary reviews.
  • Relocation assistance available.
  • Long-term potential to buy into the business and progress towards ownership.

About You

  • Registered Pharmacist eligible to practise in New Zealand.
  • Ideally 2+ years' pharmacy experience.
  • Confident in dispensing and providing quality patient care.
  • A team player who enjoys working in a friendly, collaborative environment.
  • Interested in developing professionally and potentially taking on additional responsibility.
  • Previous management experience would be beneficial but is not essential.
  • Someone with initiative who enjoys contributing ideas and improving pharmacy services.

Why Ashburton?
Ashburton offers a welcoming community, a more relaxed lifestyle and an affordable alternative to the larger cities, while still providing easy access to Christchurch and the wider Canterbury region. Whether you're an experienced Pharmacist looking for your next leadership opportunity or someone ready to take the next step in your career, this is an opportunity to grow with an independent pharmacy that genuinely values its people.

job.title: Clinical Nurse Manager
job.description:
Bring your clinical expertise, your ideas and your ability to bring people together. This is an opportunity to make a lasting difference to residents and the team caring for them.



About the organisation

This independently owned, established aged care provider in Hastings delivers rest home and hospital-level care, with a strong commitment to residents’ dignity, independence and wellbeing.

Holistic care is central to its approach. Te Whare Tapa Whā guides practice, recognising the physical, emotional, spiritual and whānau connections that help people live well. The team takes pride in providing a culturally safe, inclusive environment where residents’ identities, beliefs and choices are respected.

There is a willingness to invest in care beyond the essentials. Preventative wellness clinics, specialist wound care, exercise programmes and an on-site wellness centre reflect a commitment to helping residents enjoy the best possible quality of life.

About the role

Reporting to the Facility Manager, you will lead clinical care across a 62-bed service, supporting a capable RN team and the wider care team to deliver safe, consistent, person and whānau-centred care.

Your leadership will set the tone. By listening, communicating clearly and recognising good work, you will build confidence, strengthen collaboration and create a shared sense of direction.

There is scope to shape the role and put your ideas into practice. Planned developments include additional beds and technology to support bedside documentation, creating opportunities to improve how care is delivered.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Coaching and developing the clinical team, building a culture of respect, learning and accountability.
  • Overseeing clinical assessments, care planning and care delivery for residents with varied and sometimes complex needs.
  • Leading quality improvement, clinical risk management and ongoing audit readiness.
  • Embedding culturally safe practice and protecting residents’ rights.
  • Working closely with residents, whānau, GPs and allied health professionals.
  • Leading change and strengthening systems, processes and follow-through.
  • This is a full-time position with a share of the on-call roster.


About you

You are an experienced clinical leader who combines sound judgement with warmth, approachability and clear expectations. You enjoy developing others, welcome ideas from your team and know how to turn improvement plans into everyday practice.

You will bring:

  • New Zealand Registered Nurse registration and a current Annual Practising Certificate.
  • Aged residential care experience and at least two years’ experience leading clinical teams.
  • Strong knowledge of quality, compliance and audit requirements, including Ngā Paerewa and the ARRC agreement.
  • interRAI competency and confidence using electronic clinical systems.
  • A commitment to Te Tiriti o Waitangi, culturally safe care and Te Whare Tapa Whā.
  • Experience leading change, with the organisation and initiative to see things through.
  • Above all, you will value the people around you - residents, whānau and colleagues - and understand the difference thoughtful leadership makes.



Benefits

  • $115,000 base salary.
  • KPI-based bonus, paid in quarterly instalments and linked to agreed measures
  • Support from an experienced Facility Manager, capable RNs with clinical portfolios and an experienced quality advisor.
  • Scope to influence clinical practice, introduce improvements and grow with the service.
  • On-site gym and wellness activities.
  • Staff meals and puppy daycare.

Ready to bring your leadership to a service where you can make a visible difference? Apply now, or contact Jeanette Rendle at RWR Health for a confidential conversation.
job.salary: + quarterly bonus based on agreed measures

job.title: Care Home Manager | Dementia & Psychogeriatric Care
job.description:
About the organisation

Our client is an established national aged care provider entering an exciting chapter of growth. Their recently announced agreement to acquire another provider will expand their network to 55 care homes and 28 retirement villages, making them New Zealand’s second-largest aged care provider.

This brings greater scale, capability and opportunities to support older New Zealanders. For you, it means access to a broad network of expertise and resources, while leading a home with an important role in its local community.

About the role

This 69-bed Hastings care home provides specialist dementia and psychogeriatric care across three secure wings. Its residents need more than well-managed services. They need a leader who understands complex care, champions dignity and helps staff respond with patience, confidence and compassion.

The vacancy follows a previous manager’s internal promotion to another facility in the region. You’ll have an experienced colleague nearby who knows the home and its community. Together, you’ll support a continuum of care for residents as their needs change.

Reporting to the Regional Manager and working closely with the Clinical Service Manager, you’ll oversee the home’s people, operations, quality and financial performance.

Growing occupancy is a key priority. You’ll build strong relationships with referral partners and help families feel informed and supported when considering specialist care for their loved one.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Supporting person and whānau centred care that respects residents’ individuality, preferences and dignity.
  • Leading and developing staff working with complex cognitive, mental health and behavioural needs.
  • Building relationships with needs assessment teams, hospital services, psychogeriatric specialists, GPs and community partners.
  • Managing enquiries, referrals and admissions to improve occupancy and ensure appropriate placements.
  • Overseeing budgets, staffing, rosters and resources without compromising care quality.
  • Working alongside clinical leadership on quality improvement, risk management, audit readiness and compliance.
  • Maintaining a visible, responsive presence for residents, whānau and staff.

About you

This role calls for someone who understands the responsibility - and the privilege of leading specialist dementia and psychogeriatric care.

You’ll bring calm judgement, emotional maturity and the ability to support people through challenging situations. You’ll recognise that a resident’s behaviour can communicate an unmet need, and help your team respond thoughtfully and respectfully.

A Registered Nurse background is preferred. Experienced non-clinical care home managers will also be considered, provided they bring a strong understanding of this specialist environment and work confidently alongside clinical leaders.

You’ll also offer:

  • Leadership experience in dementia, psychogeriatric or a closely related complex care setting.
  • Strong people management skills, including coaching, performance management and team development.
  • Commercial acumen and confidence managing budgets and improving occupancy.
  • The ability to build referral networks and maintain stakeholder confidence.
  • Sensitive, clear communication with families navigating difficult decisions.
  • A commitment to culturally responsive care, resident wellbeing and staff safety.

Benefits

  • Attractive salary package and incentives circa $140k
  • Monday - Friday roster with some flexibility and on-call responsibilities as required.
  • Support from an experienced clinical team, regional leadership and national specialists.
  • Local support
  • Opportunities for development within a growing national organisation.
  • Discounts with a range of leading retailers.
  • An Immigration New Zealand Accredited Employer.
  • A rewarding leadership role in Hawke’s Bay.

Bring your experience to a home where it matters.

For a copy of the Job Description, or a confidential conversation, please contact Jeanette Rendle, Agency Director RWR Health ph 027 705 7079

job.description:
This is a part-time position on a 0.6 FTE roster, and previous palliative care nursing experience is essential.

Join a growing team in a highly regarded hospice that supports the community and their whanau in a very sensitive time. With multiple programmes available, they are making a positive impact ono how this type of care is delivered to our loved ones.

What’s in it for you

  • Competitive salary
  • Part-time hours on a 0.6 FTE roster, with flexibility around how shifts are arranged
  • Professional development opportunities to build on your palliative care experience
  • A multidisciplinary team focused on providing thoughtful care to patients and whānau

About the role
You’ll care for people living with life-limiting illness, helping manage symptoms and providing comfort as their needs change. You’ll also support whānau through difficult conversations and help them understand what to expect as someone approaches the end of life.

You’ll assess patients, recognise changes in their condition and respond to symptoms such as pain, breathlessness and nausea. You’ll work with the wider team to adapt care plans around each patient’s goals and preferences, and provide clear documentation and handovers so care stays consistent across shifts.

What you’ll bring

  • You will be a New Zealand Registered Nurse and hold a current Annual Practising Certificate
  • Previous palliative care nursing experience in a hospice, hospital or community setting where caring for palliative patients was a regular part of your work
  • Confidence in symptom assessment and management, with sound judgement about when to escalate concerns
  • A calm, culturally responsive approach to working with patients and whānau
  • Availability to work a 0.6 FTE roster

job.title: General Practitioner
job.description:
About RWR Health & General Practice
At RWR Health, we connect exceptional healthcare professionals with organisations that genuinely align with their career goals, values and lifestyle.
We take the time to understand what you're looking for and connect you with opportunities where you can develop professionally, feel supported and make a meaningful difference to the communities you serve.

We are currently looking to connect with a GPEP3 Registrar or Fellowed General Practitioner interested in joining an established, community-focused Primary Care practice in South Auckland.

What makes this opportunity particularly interesting is the flexibility around how you shape your contribution. Whether your passion lies firmly in clinical practice and delivering excellent patient care, or you're looking to continue developing your leadership experience, there is room to explore both directions.

The Opportunity
You'll be joining an established General Practice serving a predominantly Māori and Pasifika community, working alongside an experienced team of GPs and a wider multidisciplinary healthcare team.

We recognise that not every GP wants the same thing from their career. Some are happiest focusing on their patients, developing strong clinical relationships and contributing through the quality of care they deliver. Others enjoy having a broader influence, supporting colleagues, sharing their experience and helping shape the future direction of a practice.

This opportunity can accommodate either approach.

Two Potential Pathways – One Great Opportunity
1. Clinical Focus | Make Your Impact Through Patient Care
If your preference is to focus on the clinical side of General Practice, you'll have the opportunity to:

  • Deliver high-quality, patient-centred care within an established Primary Care environment.
  • Build meaningful relationships with patients and whānau.
  • Work alongside experienced GPs and a supportive multidisciplinary team.
  • Contribute your clinical knowledge and experience to the wider practice.
  • Continue developing your own clinical interests and professional goals.

2. Clinical Leadership | Help Shape the Future of the Practice
If leadership is something you enjoy, or an area you'd like to continue developing, there is an opportunity to bring your experience and perspective to the wider practice.

You'll have the opportunity to work alongside an experienced team of GPs, helping articulate the practice's clinical direction and future development.

This is not necessarily about stepping into a traditional management position. Instead, you could become a trusted clinical advisor and source of support to the Practice Manager and wider health network.

Your contribution could include:

  • Providing clinical insight and guidance to support the Practice Manager.
  • Working alongside the GP team to identify opportunities for clinical improvement and development.
  • Helping shape the practice's future direction, standards and approach to patient care.
  • Supporting collaboration across the wider healthcare network.
  • Bringing your own leadership style, experience and clinical perspective to the team.

Importantly, the level of leadership involvement is something we would look to shape around your interests, experience and aspirations.

Your New Environment
The practice is part of a wider New Zealand healthcare organisation, providing access to a broader network of knowledge, experience and support.

However, what makes this structure appealing is that each clinic retains its own identity, personality and reputation. The direction of the practice is shaped by the people within it and the community it serves.

Rather than a centralised office dictating every change or setting a one-size-fits-all approach across the network, there is an emphasis on local ownership of the practice's identity, clinical approach and progression.

You'll be joining an organisation driven by patient outcomes and a genuine reflection of the communities its clinics serve.

Within this particular practice, you'll find an experienced GP team, a strong community focus and an opportunity to contribute to the continued development of an established service.

About You
We're interested in connecting with a GPEP3 Registrar or Fellowed General Practitioner who is passionate about delivering quality Primary Care and wants to be part of a supportive, collaborative team.

You'll ideally bring:

  • GPEP3 training or Fellowship with the RNZCGP.
  • Eligibility for registration and a current practising certificate in New Zealand.
  • A genuine passion for General Practice and patient-centred care.
  • Strong clinical assessment and decision-making skills.
  • Excellent communication and relationship-building abilities.
  • A collaborative approach to working with colleagues and multidisciplinary teams.
  • An appreciation for culturally responsive healthcare and the needs of Māori and Pasifika communities.
  • An interest in contributing to the ongoing development of the practice, whether clinically or through leadership.
  • Also, for those looking for a blend of on-site and virtual settings to support your preferred way of working, all of this is possible within this organisation.

For those interested in the leadership pathway, previous experience supporting colleagues, contributing to clinical direction or working in a leadership capacity would be advantageous.

Most importantly, we're looking for someone who wants to make a positive contribution and sees value in being part of a practice where their voice, experience and approach can genuinely make a difference.

Your Next Step
Whether you're a GPEP3 looking to establish yourself in an established Primary Care environment, a Fellow wanting to focus on clinical practice, or someone ready to explore a broader leadership contribution, this is an opportunity worth a conversation.

The direction isn't predetermined. We'd like to understand what you're looking for and explore how the role could align with your strengths, interests and longer-term career goals.

If this sounds like something you'd be interested in exploring, I'd love to hear from you.

job.title: Youth Worker
job.description:
Bring your experience, build lasting relationships and become part of a community where your commitment matters.
Exclusive to RWR Health, we're partnering with Red Centre Support Services to recruit approximately 10 permanent Youth Workers for residential care services in Mount Isa, Queensland.
We're looking for people who will make the move, get involved in community life and provide consistent care. This is not a FIFO role or a fixed-term opportunity. We are looking for people who are committed to staying, building meaningful relationships and settling into both the work and the community.

The service and the young people
Red Centre provides 24/7 residential care for 26 children and young people aged 2–17 who have experienced complex trauma and require safety, stability and consistent adult support.

The service operates across nine residential houses, each accommodating up to four young people, depending on their individual circumstances and complexity of needs. Each house has a dedicated Team Leader, with most coming from teaching or youth work backgrounds.

The young people are predominantly from the Mount Isa community, and their whānau and families remain involved in their lives. Building and maintaining positive family relationships is a crucial part of the work. You'll need to understand the importance of family connection, work respectfully alongside whānau and recognise that supporting a young person also means recognising the wider relationships and community around them.

The young people have a range of complex backgrounds and support needs, which may include experiences of neglect, domestic and family violence, and sexual violence. Some also have additional learning and developmental needs, including ADHD, Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and developmental delays.
Challenging behaviours can be part of the day-to-day environment. You'll need to be confident, patient and emotionally resilient, with the ability to recognise triggers, respond appropriately to escalation and maintain a safe, consistent and supportive environment.

Much of the work happens through everyday life: preparing meals, supporting routines, attending appointments, encouraging positive activities and helping young people develop trust and confidence.

Culturally respectful care is central to the role. Many of the young people are Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander, so you'll need to listen, learn and recognise the importance of identity, family, kinship, community and connection to Country.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Building trusting relationships and providing consistent, trauma-informed care.
  • Supporting daily routines, activities, appointments and individual care plans.
  • Helping children and young people develop practical skills, confidence and independence.
  • Building positive relationships with families and whānau and recognising their importance in each young person's life.
  • Recognising triggers and responding proactively to distress, complex needs and challenging behaviours.
  • Managing behavioural escalation while maintaining safety, appropriate boundaries and a calm approach.
  • Following individual safety plans, responding to incidents and maintaining accurate records.
  • Working alongside your Team Leader, colleagues and other services to support each young person's wellbeing.

What you'll bring
We're keen to hear from people with experience supporting young people in residential care, community services, mental health, alcohol and other drugs, youth justice or related settings.

Relevant qualifications may include Youth Work, Community Services, Mental Health, Alcohol and Other Drugs, Child, Youth and Family Intervention, Social Work, Counselling or Psychology. New Zealand qualifications will need to be assessed for recognition, and we'll help clarify whether your training meets the requirements.
You'll also need:

  • An understanding of trauma-informed care, child safety and professional boundaries.
  • Confidence supporting children and young people with complex trauma, developmental needs and challenging behaviours.
  • The emotional resilience and sound judgement to manage difficult situations, including behavioural escalation.
  • Strong relationship-building skills and an appreciation of the importance of family and whānau involvement.
  • Cultural awareness and a willingness to learn about Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities, culture and connection to Country.
  • A current, valid driver's licence.
  • Current First Aid and CPR certification, or willingness to obtain these before starting.
  • The ability to meet Queensland's Blue Card, screening and mandatory training requirements.
  • NZ Citizenship (or Australian work rights).

The service operates around the clock, so flexibility across days, evenings, overnight shifts, sleepovers, weekends and public holidays is essential.

Life in Mount Isa
Mount Isa is a remote, rural mining town in outback Queensland. While it has everything you need for day-to-day living, including supermarkets, shops, healthcare services, schools, sporting facilities, community groups, restaurants and local amenities, it's important to understand that this is a very different lifestyle from living in a major city.

The town has a strong mining and regional community feel, and getting involved in local sport, volunteering or community activities can be a great way to meet people and establish yourself.

The climate is another important consideration. Summers in Mount Isa are extremely hot, with temperatures regularly reaching very high levels. You'll need to be comfortable living and working in significant heat and prepared for the demands of an outback Queensland climate.

For those who enjoy the outdoors, there are opportunities for fishing, picnics at Lake Moondarra, local sporting activities and exploring the wider region.

This opportunity will suit someone who is genuinely open to a rural lifestyle, enjoys being part of a close-knit community and is prepared to make a longer-term commitment to both the role and the area.

Pay and support for your move

On offer is:

  • Flights to support your relocation
  • Three months' free accommodation
  • Access to a shared vehicle at the accommodation
  • Assistance finding a rental as you get established
  • Supported induction including cultural training and supervised buddy shifts
  • Opportunities to develop towards team leadership or management
  • Meaningful work supporting vulnerable young people
  • Permanent, full-time employment with fortnightly pay. This could range from $97,136 - $148,075 (base rate per annum) + 12% Super and will be confirmed based on the applicable award classification and pay point based on your qualifications and experience.
  • Shift penalties and allowances, including sleepovers are on top

job.title: Youth Worker
job.description:
Bring your experience, build lasting relationships and become part of a community where your commitment matters.

Exclusive to RWR Health, we're partnering with Red Centre Support Services to recruit approximately 10 permanent Youth Workers for residential care services in Mount Isa, Queensland.

We're looking for people who will make the move, get involved in community life and provide consistent care. This is not a FIFO role or a fixed term opportunity. We are looking for a commitment to tenure and time to build relationships and settle into both the work and the community.

The work and the young people

Red Centre provides 24/7 residential care for vulnerable children and young people from 2 to 17 years old, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islanders who have experienced complex trauma and need safety, stability and adults they can trust.

Much of the work happens through everyday life: preparing meals, supporting routines, getting to appointments etc... Culturally respectful care is central to the role. You'll need to listen, learn and recognise the importance of identity, family, kinship, community and connection to Country. Your responsibilities will include:

  • Building trusting relationships and providing consistent, trauma informed care
  • Supporting daily routines, activities, appointments and individual care plans
  • Helping children and young people develop practical skills, confidence and independence
  • Recognising triggers and responding proactively to distress and changing behaviour
  • Following individual safety plans, responding to incidents and maintaining accurate records
  • Working alongside your team and other services to support each young person's wellbeing


What you'll bring

We’re keen to hear from people with experience supporting young people in residential care, community services, mental health, alcohol and other drugs, youth justice or related settings.

Relevant qualifications may include Youth Work, Community Services, Mental Health, Alcohol and Other Drugs, Child, Youth and Family Intervention, Social Work, Counselling or Psychology. New Zealand qualifications will need to be assessed for recognition and we'll help clarify whether your training meets the requirements.

You’ll also need:

  • An understanding of trauma-informed care, child safety and professional boundaries.
  • The confidence to manage challenging situations with empathy and sound judgement.
  • A current, valid driver’s licence.
  • Current First Aid and CPR certification, or willingness to obtain these before starting.
  • The ability to meet Queensland’s Blue Card, screening and mandatory training requirements.
  • NZ Citizenship (or Australian work rights)

The service operates around the clock, so flexibility across days, evenings, overnight shifts, sleepovers, weekends and public holidays is essential.

Life in Mount Isa

Mount Isa would suit someone who enjoys community life, sport and the outdoors. Getting involved in a club, volunteering or joining local activities can help you meet people and feel at home.

There are sporting clubs, community groups, local events and a movie theatre. Days off might include fishing or a picnic at Lake Moondarra, a game with a local sports team, or exploring the wider region.

  • Supported induction including cultural training and supervised buddy shifts
